caveats: Sirloin varies by grade, marbling, external-fat trim, and cooking loss; this entry represents the named raw USDA identity rather than every steak sold as sirloin.

closing.summary: Best bits are complete, highly usable protein, vitamin B12, zinc, and being an easy whole-cut meal anchor. Weak spots are the middling fat profile, low potassium, thin vitamin range, and how much the trim changes the result. Best for muscle-focused meals and practical dinners because it gives you serious protein without processed-meat baggage. Pair it with vegetables and a fibre-rich carb, and keep an eye on the fat trim.

scenes.narrationText: 12.7 grams of fat. Cholesterol is 75 milligrams, which is a fairly controlled mark for a meat. Polyunsaturated fat is only 0.48 grams, so very little of the fat comes from that more heart-friendly type. Saturated fat is 5.2 grams, which adds some real baggage. For meats, the fat mix decides how much baggage comes with the protein.

scenes.narrationText: 20.4 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score 9 out of 9. That means all nine amino acids your body cannot make on its own show up in useful amounts, helping muscle repair and maintenance. Collagen is only 1.6 grams, so sirloin is not doing much on that structural-protein side. For meats, usable complete protein is the main job, and sirloin nails that part.

scenes.narrationText: Vitamin B12 is 44% daily value. B12 helps your nerves work properly and helps make red blood cells, which carry oxygen around the body. The rest of the vitamin panel is very quiet. For meats, B12 is a real strength, but one strong vitamin does not equal broad vitamin coverage.

scenes.narrationText: Zinc is 32% daily value, a strong amount for immune function and wound healing. Potassium is only 7% daily value, so it does not bring much help with fluid balance or normal muscle function. Iron is 9% daily value, useful but smaller than beef's reputation might suggest. For meats, zinc and iron can add value beyond protein, and zinc does most of that work here.

Add vegetables and a carb and dinner is basically sorted. Works across plenty of simple meals. Grill it, pan-sear it, slice it into wraps, or throw it into a stir-fry.
